name: Chance Packs His Belongings with the TV On
description: Chance moves around the room, collecting his personal items and placing them into a bag. The television plays in the background, casting flickering light across the walls as he works quietly, methodically, folding clothes and tucking small objects into pockets and zippers.
related_events: Chance packs his belongings while the TV is on

name: Chance Ascends the Stairs
description: Chance enters an enclosed stairway and begins to climb, moving steadily upward step by step.
related_events: Chance ascends the stairs in an enclosed stairway

description: Eve walks through the hallway and steps into the large glass-enclosed room.

name: Limo Arrives at Rand Estate
description: The limo approaches the entrance of the Rand Estate and slows as it reaches the open gate. Two guards stand on either side, motionless, then raise their hands in a crisp salute as the vehicle passes through.

Chance walks down the hallway

name: Chance Follows the Statue's Point
description: Chance stands at a crossroads, looking first down one street, then the other, unsure of which way to go. He turns and notices a large statue of Benito Juarez, one arm extended, pointing down a particular street. Chance watches the statue, then steps away in the direction it indicates.
related_events: Chance observes statue of Benito Juarez pointing
Chance decides to follow direction indicated by statue

name: Chance Opens the Front Door and Steps Outside
description: Chance stands at the front door, pauses, then turns the handle and opens it. He steps through, out onto the porch, and pulls the door shut behind him.
related_events: Chance hesitates before opening the front door
Chance opens the front door and steps outside

name: Chance Leaves Rear Building with Suitcase and Inspects Garden
description: Chance steps out of the rear building carrying a suitcase. As he walks toward the townhouse, he stops several times to look at his garden.
related_events: Chance exits rear building with suitcase
Chance pauses to inspect garden during walk

name: Chance Prepares the Touring Car in the Garage
description: Chance enters the garage and walks over to the touring car. He pulls the cover off the vehicle, folds it neatly, and places it on a shelf. After stepping back, he leaves the garage.
related_events: Chance uncovers the touring car in the garage
Chance folds the car cover and places it on a shelf
Chance exits the garage

name: Chance Selects Suitcase and Suit in the Attic
description: Chance entered the attic, which was filled with the Old Man's belongings. He turned on an old black-and-white television that had a magnifying lens attached to the front. The screen lit up, casting a dim glow across the room. Nearby, several suitcases sat together. Chance picked one—a fine leather suitcase—from among them. He then walked to a long rack lined with clothing and took down a handmade suit.
related_events: Chance enters the attic and turns on an old black-and-white TV
Chance selects a fine leather suitcase from several available
Chance removes a handmade suit from a long rack

name: Chance Performs Routine Care and Exits
description: Chance enters the room, turns on the television, which displays a spinning color wheel. He picks up a sprinkling can and waters several potted plants. Afterward, he turns off the television and leaves the room.

Chance waters several potted plants with a sprinkling can
Chance turns off the television and leaves the room

description: Chance returns to his room and changes the channel on the television. He takes off his robe and hangs it in the closet. Then he walks into the bathroom.

Chance removes and hangs up his robe
Chance enters the bathroom from his room

name: Chance Approaches a Street Group and Leaves
description: Chance rounds the corner and walks toward a group of Black people huddled around a fire on the sidewalk, their bodies pressed into threadbare furniture. He stops near them and smiles. The group stares back without moving or returning the gesture. Chance nods politely, then turns and walks down the sidewalk, away from the fire.
related_events: Chance approaches a group of people huddled around a fire
Chance smiles and receives no friendly response
Chance nods politely and walks away

name: Chance Completes Evening Routine and Exits Bedroom
description: The TV plays softly from offstage as Chance finishes washing up in the bathroom. He walks into the bedroom, opens his closet, and takes out a pair of house slippers. After putting them on, he walks over to the television, turns it off, and leaves the room.

Chance retrieves house slippers from his closet
Chance turns off the television
Chance leaves the bedroom

name: Cover the Touring Car and Leave the Garage
description: Chance enters the garage from the garden as the music grows louder. A 1921 TOURING CAR comes into view as he walks through the space. He takes a neatly folded cover from a shelf and drapes it carefully over the car. Once the car is covered, he picks up the pitchfork and exits the garage through a side entry.

Chance reveals 1921 TOURING CAR by walking through garage
Chance covers car with protective cover for the night
Chance leaves garage through side entry with pitchfork

name: Chance Locked Out in a Decaying Neighborhood
description: Chance steps out onto the front steps of the townhouse and pauses, taking in the ruined neighborhood around him. The snow is stained grey, the neighboring houses have broken windows and are covered in graffiti. He turns back toward the townhouse, reaches for the door, but finds it locked. He stands still for a moment on the sidewalk cluttered with trash, then moves off to his left.

Chance finds the townhouse door locked behind him
Chance decides on a direction and departs from the townhouse steps

name: Chance Answers Questions and Prepares to Leave
description: Franklin asks Chance if he has served in the Army. Chance replies that he has not, but has seen the Army on television. Hayes then asks about taxes, wondering if Chance has ever paid them. Chance says no. He picks up his slippers, puts on his snow-boots, and leads Franklin and Hayes outside.

Hayes questions Chance about tax payments
Chance puts on his snow-boots before leaving
Chance picks up his slippers and exits with the attorneys

name: Chance Reads Bulletin Board and Smiles in Chinatown
description: Chance stands in front of a bulletin board affixed to a storefront in Chinatown, looking at the notes pinned to it. The notes are written in Chinese, and he reads them quietly. After a moment, he smiles, then turns away and walks on through the neighborhood.
related_events: Chance reads notes on bulletin board in Chinatown
Chance smiles after viewing bulletin board
Chance walks away from bulletin board through Chinatown

name: Chance Shows Franklin and Hayes the Touring Car and His Room
description: Franklin and Hayes look at the touring car with surprise. Franklin asks Chance if he drives it. Chance says no, that he has never been in an automobile. Hayes reacts with amazement. Chance pauses, then admits he has sat in the car from time to time, but only inside the garage. He adds that the car hasn't been outside since the Old Man hurt himself. He turns and says he lives in there now. Chance walks toward his room, and Franklin and Hayes follow.
related_events: Franklin and Hayes express surprise at the touring car
Chance reveals he has rarely used the automobile
Chance leads Franklin and Hayes to his room

name: Chance Asks Elderly Woman for Lunch
description: On a street lined with adult bookstores, X-rated movie theaters, and strip clubs, an elderly Black woman walks carrying a bag of groceries. Chance steps in front of her, blocking her path. He says, 'I'm very hungry now. Would you please bring me my lunch?' The woman looks up at him, her expression shifting to fear. Without responding, she turns and half-runs into a nearby sleazy bar. Chance watches her go, then continues walking down the street.
related_events: Chance stops elderly woman on street lined with adult establishments
Chance requests lunch from elderly woman
Elderly woman flees into sleazy bar out of fear
Chance continues walking after woman flees

name: Eve Misinterprets Chance's Channel Switching
description: Chance sits in front of the television, flipping channels until he lands on the news and watches it. Eve observes him and remarks that she admires his interest in staying informed. Chance nods silently and changes the channel again, now watching a Mighty Mouse cartoon. Eve looks at him with confusion, then smiles, as if she believes he switched to the cartoon on purpose to amuse her.

Eve interprets Chance's TV watching as intellectual engagement
Chance changes channel to watch a Mighty Mouse cartoon
Eve misinterprets cartoon viewing as a humorous gesture

name: Chance Tries to Join the Game
description: Chance stands by a chain-link fence, watching a group of teenage boys play basketball. He bangs on the fence and calls out to them. 'I have seen your game! I have watched Elvin Hayes play it many times! They call him "Big E!"' The boys continue playing, not responding or looking his way. After a moment, Chance turns and walks away from the court.

Chance bangs on the fence and calls out to the boys
Chance references Elvin Hayes and compares the boys' game to 'Big E'

Chance walks away from the basketball court

name: Chance Reports a Sick Tree to a Policeman Near the White House
description: Tourists stand near the fence of the White House, looking toward the building. Chance turns away from the group and examines the branches of a dying tree. He walks over to a policeman standing nearby and points at the tree. "That tree is very sick," he says. "It should be cared for." The policeman glances at the tree, then at Chance, and nods. "Yes sir. I'll report it right away." Chance replies, "Yes. That would be a good thing to do. Good day." The policeman says, "Good day," and takes out his walkie-talkie as Chance walks away.
related_events: Chance observes a dying tree near the White House
Chance advises a policeman about the sick tree
Policeman agrees to report the condition of the tree
Policeman uses walkie-talkie to report tree condition

name: Chance Enters the Building and Hangs Up His Umbrella
description: Chance opens the door, steps inside, and closes the umbrella. He shakes it off, then hangs it on a doorknob before walking toward the dining room.

Chance hangs umbrella on doorknob

name: Chance Walks to the Dining Room
description: Chance closes the umbrella, hangs it on a doorknob, and walks from the entry area to the dining room.
related_events: Chance walks to the dining room

name: Chance crosses to the main house with an umbrella
description: A light snow is falling. The door to the small building opens, and Chance peers out. He steps back inside, closing the door behind him. A moment later, the door opens again, and Chance emerges holding an umbrella. Dressed in a suit and tie, he walks across the snowy ground toward the main house.

Chance exits the small building with an umbrella

name: Chance Walks to the Main House in the Snow
description: A light snow is falling. The door of the small building opens, and Chance peers out before stepping back inside. A moment later, he emerges again, now holding an umbrella. Dressed in a suit and tie, he crosses the snowy ground and makes his way to the main house.

name: Chance Finishes Gardening and Heads to the Outbuilding
description: In the late afternoon, with the trees bare and dusk settling over the garden, Chance worked the soil along the walkway, turning the loam with careful attention. He paused, withdrew a pocket watch from his coat, and checked the time. Above him, the sky deepened with the approach of evening. He closed the watch and began walking toward the one-story brick building at the far end of the garden. As he walked, he pulled a clean rag from his apron pocket and wiped the dirt from the tines of his pitchfork.

Chance checks the time with his pocket watch
Chance observes the darkening skies
Chance begins walking toward the one story brick building
Chance wipes the pitchfork tines with a rag

name: Chance Wakes and Turns on the TV
description: Chance lies on his back, asleep. His eyes open slowly. Without changing his expression, he sits up, picks up the remote control, and turns on the television. He remains on the bed, watching the screen.
related_events: Chance wakes up and sits up in bed
Chance turns on the television with the remote control

name: Chance Prepares to Leave the Bedroom
description: Chance sits up in bed and turns on the TV with the remote. He gets up, walks to the dresser, and takes a pocket watch from the drawer, glancing at the time. Without looking away from the television, he crosses the room to the closet, puts on a bathrobe, and leaves.
related_events: Chance leaves the bedroom
Chance puts on a bathrobe
Chance checks the time on his pocket watch

name: Chance Oils a Pitchfork While Watching the Boston Pops
description: Chance stands in the Potting Room, carefully oiling the tines of a pitchfork. Around him, rows of small pots line the tables, some holding young sprouting plants. A 1940s black-and-white television plays on a shelf, its screen showing the Boston Pops Orchestra. A spinning wheel with colored gels attached to the front of the set casts shifting hues, creating the illusion of color. As the music plays, Chance watches the broadcast, his movements deliberate. After finishing with the pitchfork, he places it back in its storage spot. He turns off the television before leaving the room, but the sound of the orchestra continues to fill the space.
related_events: Chance oils pitchfork tines and stores the tool
Chance watches television while performing gardening tool maintenance

name: Chance Turns Off the Television
description: Chance stands in the Potting Room, watching the small black-and-white television with the spinning color gel wheel attached to its screen. The Boston Pops Orchestra plays on the broadcast. He reaches out, turns the television off. The image on the screen disappears, but the music continues to fill the room. He steps away and leaves the room behind.
related_events: Chance turns off television in the Potting Room

name: Eve Hands Over Care and Leaves for Mr. Rand
description: Once inside the house, Wilson took over wheeling Chance. A woman named Greta stepped forward to take Eve's coat. Eve thanked her, then told Wilson she would be with Mr. Rand if needed. She turned to Chance and said she would see him after the doctor had examined his leg. Chance, looking around the mansion, agreed that the doctor should check his leg. Eve watched as Wilson wheeled Chance around a corner and out of sight.

Eve tells Chance she will see him after the doctor examines his leg

name: Wilson Wheels Chance Through the Mansion
description: Wilson takes the wheelchair and begins guiding Chance through the house. As they move, Chance looks around the mansion and remarks that the doctor should examine his leg. Wilson continues wheeling him, turning a corner and disappearing from Eve's view.

name: Louise Leaves After the Old Man's Body Is Carried Out
description: Louise enters the hallway and picks up her suitcases from beside the door. She pauses as she sees two men in white clothes carrying a stretcher down the main staircase. The Old Man's body lies covered on it. She watches them descend, noting how easily they manage the weight. 'He used to be a big man... 'Spose he wasted away to about nothin'...' she says quietly. After a moment, she steps toward the stretcher bearers. 'Wait up! I'm goin' out that door first,' she tells them. She gives the covered body one last look, then opens the front door and walks out.
related_events: Louise picks up suitcases by the door
Two men in white carry Old Man's body down staircase
Louise reflects on Old Man's physical decline

name: Louise Leaves the House
description: Louise stands in the hallway, holding a couple of suitcases. She looks at the Old Man’s body on the stretcher as two men in white carry it down the staircase. She says quietly, 'He used to be a big man... 'Spose he wasted away to about nothin'...' Then, speaking directly to the body, she says, 'I guess I'll be goin' off to find me some folks, Old Man... I'm not batty enough to stay around this neighborhood any longer...' The men approach the front door with the stretcher. Louise steps in front of them and says, 'Wait up! I'm goin' out that door first.' She turns, gives one last look at the covered body, opens the front door, and walks out.
related_events: Louise announces departure to Old Man's body
Louise blocks stretcher bearers at the front door
Louise exits through the front door after final glance at body

name: Franklin and Hayes Arrive at the House
description: A key turns in the lock, and the door opens. Thomas Franklin and Sally Hayes step inside, carrying briefcases. Hayes looks around, her expression shifting with surprise. "This is another world, Tom," she says. "I never would have believed it." Franklin nods. "Yeah... He and my father used to ride together back in the thirties. Fox hunting. Before I was born." She asks if he’ll give her a tour. "Gladly," he replies, smiling. He places a hand on her shoulder as they walk down the hall.
related_events: Thomas Franklin and Sally Hayes enter the house
Sally Hayes expresses surprise at the house interior

name: Franklin Shares Family History of the House
description: Thomas Franklin and Sally Hayes enter the house. Hayes looks around, surprised by the interior. She remarks that the place feels like another world. Franklin nods and explains that the house owner and his father used to ride together in the 1930s, fox hunting before he was born. He smiles and offers to give her a tour, mentioning that the safe is in Mr. Jennings' bedroom and that it will be their first stop. He places a hand on her shoulder as they walk down the hall together.
related_events: Thomas Franklin recounts family history with house owner

name: Thomas Franklin and Sally Hayes Begin a Tour of the House
description: Sally Hayes looks around the interior and expresses surprise at the appearance of the house. She asks Thomas Franklin if he will give her a tour. Franklin agrees and says he will start by showing her Mr. Jennings' bedroom, where the safe is located. As they walk down the hall, Franklin places his hand on Hayes' shoulder.

Thomas Franklin agrees to give a tour of the house
Thomas Franklin places hand on Sally Hayes' shoulder while walking down the hall

name: Chance Enters the TV Room and Changes Channels
description: Chance entered the room adjacent to the Potting Room. A large screen remote control color television was on, tuned to the Boston Pops. He stood and watched the screen with a detached gaze while removing his apron. Using the remote control, he changed the channel. He placed the apron and the pitchfork rag into a laundry bag. He took off his suit jacket and hung it in the closet, where several other jackets of similar quality were already hanging. He changed the channel again.
related_events: Chance enters the room adjacent to the Potting Room
Chance watches television with detached gaze
Chance changes television channel using remote control

name: Chance Changes from Work to Rest
description: Chance removes his apron and places it along with a pitchfork rag into a laundry bag. He takes off his suit jacket and hangs it in the closet, where several other jackets of similar quality already hang. He stands in the room as the television plays, the screen shifting as he changes the channel.

Chance removes suit jacket and hangs it in closet

name: Chance Changes the Channel Again
description: After finishing his routine, Chance entered the room adjacent to the Potting Room, where a large color television set was playing the Boston Pops. He stood before it, watching with a detached gaze as he removed his apron. Using the remote control, he changed the channel. He placed the apron and a pitchfork rag into a laundry bag, then took off his suit jacket and hung it in the closet among several others of similar quality. He changed the channel once more.

Chance turns on the television and places a napkin on his lap

name: Chance Searches for Louise and Continues Watching TV
description: Chance sits in his chair, watching television with a napkin on his lap. After a moment, he turns his head, looking around for Louise. Not seeing her, he turns back to the screen and keeps watching. The program changes to a lively football game, and he focuses on the action.
related_events: Chance looks for Louise but resumes watching TV when she does not appear

name: Chance Watches Football, Then Switches to News
description: Chance sits in his chair, turns on the television, and places a napkin on his lap. He flips to a channel showing a loud and intense football game, watching for a moment. At a peak moment in the game, he changes the channel. The screen now shows the President of the United States greeting foreign dignitaries at the White House. Close-up shots display the President using a two-handed handshake with each guest. Chance silently watches, then unconsciously grips one hand with the other.
related_events: Chance changes channels to view a highly energetic football game
Chance switches channels to watch U.S. President greeting foreign dignitaries

name: Chance Mimics the President's Handshake
description: Chance sits in his chair, watching the television as the President greets foreign dignitaries at the White House. On screen, the President shakes hands with each guest using both hands. As the broadcast continues, Chance looks on quietly, then slowly brings one hand up and grasps it with the other, holding the position without comment or awareness.
related_events: Chance unconsciously imitates the President's two-handed handshake gesture

name: Chance Gardens as Louise Visits
description: The snow has stopped falling. Chance, wearing a hat, a gardening apron over his suit, and boots, works quietly in the garden. Louise comes out of the main house, wrapped in a heavy coat with a scarf over her head. She approaches and greets him. Chance pauses and tips his hat to her, just as he once saw a man do on television. Louise remarks on his manners, then tells him she has to go. She says he should find someone to be with, suggesting an older woman, and gently touches his shoulder. She calls him a little boy and gives his shoulder a squeeze before turning toward the house. Chance watches her go and says goodbye. Louise waves as she steps inside. Chance tips his hat once more before returning to his work.
related_events: Chance tends to the garden in winter attire
Louise exits the main house and speaks with Chance

name: Louise Talks to Chance in the Garden
description: It had stopped snowing. Chance, wearing a hat, a gardening apron over his suit, and boots, was working in the garden. Louise came out of the main house, dressed warmly with a scarf over her head and a heavy coat. When Chance saw her, he tipped his hat to her in a polite, gentlemanly way. Louise remarked on his manners, then said she had to go. She told him he would need someone around, suggesting he find an older woman because, as she put it, he wouldn’t be of use to a young one, adding that he would always be a little boy. As she spoke, she placed her hand on his shoulder. Chance continued working, smiling slightly. Louise squeezed his shoulder, said goodbye, and walked toward the house. Chance called out goodbye, and as she went inside, he tipped his hat once more.
related_events: Chance tips his hat to Louise in a gentlemanly manner
Louise touches Chance's shoulder and speaks to him

name: Louise Says Goodbye and Leaves
description: Louise tells Chance goodbye and gently squeezes his shoulder before turning toward the house. As she reaches the townhouse, she waves. Chance lifts his hat to her one last time as she goes inside.

Chance responds to Louise as she leaves
Louise waves while entering the townhouse
Chance tips his hat to Louise one final time

name: Chance Visits the Old Man's Bedside
description: There was a polite knock at the door, then Chance entered the room. He moved slowly to the Old Man's bed and stood beside it for a moment. He reached down and gently pulled the sheet back from the Old Man's face. He touched the man's forehead lightly, then let the sheet fall back into place.
related_events: Chance enters the room after a knock
Chance uncovers the Old Man's face
Chance touches the Old Man's forehead

name: Chance Turns On the TV and Sits by the Old Man
description: After standing by the Old Man's bed and touching his forehead, Chance moves to the television and turns it on. The set is the same model as the one in his own room. He sits down in the easy chair beside the bed and rests one arm on the Old Man's covered body. With the other hand, he uses the remote control to change channels. He stops on a movie from the 1940s and watches as a man on screen tips his hat to a woman.

Chance sits in the easy chair next to the Old Man's bed

name: Chance Watches a Movie with the Old Man

He picks up the remote and changes the channel for a moment, then switches back to the film. On screen, a gentleman tips his hat to a lady. Chance watches the scene closely, his attention fixed on the image.

description: Two uniformed valets, Wilson and Perkins, stand by the entrance of the Rand mansion as a limousine pulls up. Wilson positions himself behind a wheelchair waiting near the door. As the vehicle stops, Perkins and another man named Jeffrey help Chance into the wheelchair. Wilson approaches Eve as she steps out of the limo and says, 'Good evening, Mrs. Rand.' Eve replies, 'Good evening, Wilson.' Wilson adds that he will take Chance to the third floor guest suite, where Dr. Allenby is waiting. Eve acknowledges with a thank you. Perkins and Jeffrey then wheel Chance up the steps and into the house, followed by Eve and Wilson.

Elevator doors close on Wilson and Chance

name: Chance Experiences an Elevator for the First Time
description: The doors open, and Wilson pushes Chance into the elevator. As Wilson presses a button and the doors close, Chance looks around with a puzzled expression. He turns to Wilson and says he has never been in one of these before. Wilson assumes he is referring to the wheelchair and explains that it belongs to Mr. Rand, who uses it because of his illness. Chance asks if the elevator has a television. Wilson laughs and says no, though Mr. Rand’s wheelchair has an electric motor to help him move independently. Chance nods and continues looking around the elevator, then asks how long they will stay inside. Wilson tells him he doesn’t know—it depends on what the doctor says. The elevator comes to a stop on the third floor.

name: Chance Asks About Elevator and Wheelchair
description: The elevator doors close after Wilson pushes Chance inside. A quiet moment passes as Chance looks around, then turns to Wilson. CHANCE ... I've never been in one of these. Wilson assumes he means the wheelchair. WILSON It's one of Mr. Rand's. Since he's been ill... Chance continues scanning the walls of the elevator. CHANCE Does it have a television? Wilson chuckles. WILSON No — but Mr. Rand does have one with an electric motor, that way he can get around by himself. CHANCE I see. Chance glances again at the elevator panel. CHANCE How long do we stay in here? WILSON How long? I don't know, see what the doctor says... The elevator comes to a stop on the third floor.
related_events: Chance inquires about a television in the elevator
Wilson explains Mr. Rand's motorized wheelchair

name: Chance Asks How Long They'll Stay in the Elevator

Wilson assumes he means the wheelchair and explains it belongs to Mr. Rand, used since his illness. Chance continues scanning the elevator. CHANCE Does it have a television? Wilson laughs and says no, though Mr. Rand’s wheelchair has an electric motor for independence. CHANCE I see. He looks around again. CHANCE How long do we stay in here? WILSON How long? I don't know, see what the doctor says. The elevator comes to a stop on the third floor.

name: Wilson and Chance Arrive on the Third Floor
description: The elevator slows and comes to a stop on the third floor. The doors open, revealing the hallway beyond.
related_events: Elevator comes to a stop on the third floor

name: Chance Sets the Table and Begins Dinner
description: Chance enters the dining room and places his laundry bag on a covered table near the doorway. He sits at the dining table, turns on a small portable color TV placed beside his uncovered place setting, and carefully unfolds his napkin, laying it on his lap. The dropcloth covers most of the table and chairs, but one seat remains accessible. As the television plays, Chance begins to eat the meal Louise has set before him.
related_events: Chance arrives and prepares to eat dinner at the dining room table

name: Louise Brings Dinner and Speaks of the Old Man's Decline
description: Louise enters carrying a tray with Chance's dinner and his clean laundry. She sets the meal in front of him at the uncovered place setting near the portable TV. Chance, seated at the table with a napkin on his lap, turns on the television and begins to eat. Louise places his folded clothes on the nearby table and picks up his laundry bag. She tells him the Old Man is getting weaker, slipping more with each passing hour. Chance continues eating, his eyes on the screen, and asks if the Old Man's back is feeling better. Louise gives him a look and mutters about his strange way of speaking. A buzzer sounds, and she glances toward the stairs, remarking that the Old Man needs her more often now, just before he won't need her at all. She worries about the toll the constant trips up and down the stairs are taking on her, saying she doesn't want to be taken before her time. Then she turns and leaves the room.
related_events: Louise serves Chance dinner and informs him about the Old Man's declining health
Louise expresses concern about the Old Man's deteriorating condition

name: Chance Eats While Louise Speaks of the Old Man's Decline
description: Louise enters with a tray of food and Chance's clean laundry. She sets the dinner before him and says the Old Man is getting weaker. Chance replies, 'I see,' and begins to eat. He keeps his eyes on the television as he unfolds his napkin and places it on his lap. A buzzer sounds, and Louise looks toward the stairs. She remarks that the Old Man needs her more often now, and she turns to leave, muttering about the strain of climbing the stairs. Chance asks if the Old Man's back is feeling better. Louise gives him a look and calls his speech gobbledegook before exiting.
related_events: Chance responds to Louise's comment about the Old Man

name: Chance Asks About the Old Man's Back While Watching TV
description: Chance sits at the dining table, watching a small portable TV as he eats his dinner. The table is covered with a dropcloth, and his clean laundry is placed nearby. Louise enters with his meal and collects his laundry bag. She mentions that the Old Man is getting weaker and needs her more frequently. Without looking away from the screen, Chance asks if the Old Man's back is feeling better. Louise gives him a sharp look and mutters about his confusing way of speaking, calling it 'gobbledegook.' She complains about the strain of going up and down the stairs so often and warns that she might not survive it. Then she turns and leaves the room.
related_events: Chance inquires about the Old Man's back pain
Louise reacts to Chance's detached behavior during conversation

name: Louise Answers the Buzzer for the Old Man
description: The buzzer sounds from upstairs. Louise turns toward the staircase, her expression tired. She mutters about having to go back up again, saying the Old Man needs her more often now, just before the time comes when he won’t need her at all. She comments on the strain of climbing the stairs, then leaves the room, heading upstairs.
related_events: Louise responds to an upstairs buzzer signaling the Old Man's need

name: Chance Approaches the Gang on the Corner
description: Chance walks up to a group of eight to ten youths gathered on a street corner. The group falls silent, watching him closely as he nears. He stops and speaks calmly. He asks if they know where he could find a garden to work in. He says he had to leave his garden because the Old Man has died and explains that he needs to start seeds and work the soil for spring.
related_events: Chance approaches a group of youths on a street corner
Chance explains he must find a new garden to work in

name: Abbaz Confronts Chance Over Raphael and the Old Man's Death
description: Lolo asks Chance what he grows, but before Chance can answer, Abbaz steps forward, shoving Lolo aside. He gets in Chance’s face, demanding to know what he’s doing there and accusing him of being sent by Raphael. Chance calmly replies that no one sent him, explaining that Thomas Franklin told him the Old Man had died. Abbaz refuses to believe it, insisting the Old Man isn’t dead and warning Chance not to deliver messages on Raphael’s behalf. He orders Chance to tell Raphael to come in person if he has something to say. As Abbaz presses closer, Chance reaches into his pocket, pulls out a remote control, and clicks it three times toward Abbaz, then sighs and puts it away when nothing happens. Without another word, Chance walks off, leaving the group behind.
related_events: Lolo asks Chance what he grows
Abbaz confronts Chance face to face
Abbaz accuses Chance of being a messenger for Raphael
Abbaz denies the Old Man's death and threatens Chance

name: Chance Announces the Old Man's Death
description: Chance stands before the group of youths as Abbaz looms close, demanding to know who sent him. Chance replies that Thomas Franklin told him to leave the Old Man's house because the Old Man has died. He speaks calmly, without hesitation. The gang falls silent, then stirs with murmurs. Lolo and the others exchange glances, their suspicion rising. No one moves to stop Chance as he turns and walks away, saying, "Good day."
related_events: Chance mentions Thomas Franklin and the Old Man's death

name: Chance Points Remote at Abbaz, Gang Responds with Knife
description: Chance reaches into his pocket and pulls out a remote control. He points it at Abbaz and clicks it three times, as if changing a television channel. The gesture startles the group. Abbaz reacts instantly, drawing a switchblade and snapping the blade open. He holds the knife close to Chance, demanding he leave. Chance looks down at the remote, slips it back into his pocket, and says he understands. He turns and walks away as the gang watches him go.
related_events: Chance takes out remote control and pretends to change Abbaz like a TV
Abbaz threatens Chance with switchblade after remote gesture
Chance expresses disappointment and pockets remote

name: The Gang Reacts After Chance Leaves
description: After Chance walks away, the group of youths bursts into loud, overlapping questions. One asks who the hell died. Another wonders why Chance pointed that remote control at them like a signal. The mention of the Old Man's death sparks a guess—'Must be Papa Joe.' The name hangs in the air as they look at each other, uneasy. Murmurs spread through the group, voices low and tense, piecing together what just happened. They stand rooted to the corner, talking fast, trying to make sense of the stranger, the remote, and the news no one expected.
related_events: Gang reacts with confusion and speculation after Chance leaves

name: Chance Settles Into the Room
description: Chance sits on the bed and removes his boots, then puts on a pair of slippers. He walks to the closet and opens the door, revealing rows of men's clothing. He says he is allowed to take any of the Old Man's suits, shirts, shoes, and coats, and that they all fit him well. Hayes remarks that the style of the clothes has come back into fashion. Chance turns on the television using a remote control and watches it for a moment. The room remains quiet as he stands there, looking at the screen.
related_events: Chance sits on the bed to remove his boots
Chance puts on his slippers and accesses the closet
Chance explains his access to the Old Man's clothes
Hayes comments on the resurgence of the Old Man's clothing style
Chance turns on the television with a remote control

name: Franklin and Hayes Question Chance
description: Chance sits on the bed and removes his boots while Hayes and Franklin look around the room. He turns on the television with a remote, remarking that the Old Man gave him the set and that it has remote control, just like the one the Old Man owns. Franklin tells Chance they have no information linking him to the deceased. Chance says he understands. He puts on his slippers, walks to the closet, and opens it, revealing rows of men's clothing. He explains he is allowed to go to the attic and take any of the Old Man’s suits, shirts, shoes, and coats, and that everything fits him well. Hayes comments that the clothes have come back into style. Chance says he has seen the styles on television. Franklin asks what his plans are now. Chance says he would like to stay and work in his garden. He turns to watch the television. Franklin pulls Hayes aside and asks what he thinks. Hayes says he doesn’t know—Chance seems honest and simple, even charming, but it’s bizarre, and he doesn’t know what to make of it. Franklin agrees, saying Chance is hard to figure—either very bright or very dense—and they should keep things legal. He takes papers from his briefcase and approaches Chance. Franklin says that if what Chance claims is true, he wants to know what kind of claim Chance intends to make on the estate. Chance says he’s fine, the garden is healthy, and he has no need for a claim. Franklin says that’s good and asks him to sign a release. He hands the paper to Chance, but Chance does not take it. Chance says he doesn’t know how to sign. Franklin presses him, and Chance confirms he won’t sign. Franklin says that if Chance insists on continuing this way, the house will be closed the next day at noon, and he will have to leave. Chance says he doesn’t understand. Franklin repeats that the house is closing and Chance must move out. He gives Chance his business card and tells him to call if he changes his mind. He turns to Hayes and suggests they go eat. Hayes smiles at Chance and says good day. Chance returns the smile and says good day. After they leave, Chance places the card on a desk without looking at it and turns back to watch the television.
related_events: Franklin questions Chance about his connection to the deceased
Franklin inquires about Chance's future plans
Chance expresses desire to continue working in his garden

Chance does not take the paper and says he cannot sign because he does not know how. Franklin presses him, and when Chance again refuses, Franklin tells him the house will be closed the next day at noon and that he must leave. He hands Chance his business card and says to call if he changes his mind. Franklin then turns to Hayes and suggests they go. Hayes smiles at Chance and says goodbye. Chance returns the smile, then places the card on a desk without looking at it and turns back to watch the television.

description: Franklin handed Chance his business card and told him to call if he changed his mind. Then, Franklin turned to Hayes and said it was time to go. They left the room and walked out of the house. Chance placed the business card on the desk without looking at it and sat down to watch television.

Franklin and Hayes prepare to leave the house

name: Franklin and Hayes Meet Chance in the Dining Room
description: Franklin and Hayes enter the dining room and see Chance sitting in front of the television. Franklin, surprised, greets him and introduces himself as Thomas Franklin, extending his hand. Chance remains seated but takes Franklin's hand warmly with both of his own, introducing himself as Chance, the gardener. Franklin laughs, assuming it is a joke, and introduces Hayes, who steps forward to shake Chance's hand as well. Chance greets her politely, then turns back to the TV. Franklin explains that he and Hayes are from the law firm Franklin, Jennings and Roberts, handling the estate. Chance smiles and says he understands. Franklin asks if Chance is waiting for someone, and Chance replies that he is waiting for Louise to bring him lunch. Franklin expresses confusion, noting that Louise, the maid, should have left earlier. Chance only smiles. Franklin asks what Chance is doing there, and Chance says he lives in the house. Franklin, skeptical, says they have no record of that. Chance replies that he has lived there since he was a child, always working in the garden. Hayes questions whether he is truly a gardener, noting his appearance. Chance confirms it. Franklin asks for proof of employment, such as checks or contracts, but Chance says he has none. He explains he was compensated with meals and a place to live and never needed money. Franklin asks for identification, medical records, or the name of a doctor, but Chance says he has never been ill, has never left the house, and has had no visitors except Joe Saracini, a mason who came in 1952 to repair the brickwork. Chance recalls Joe showed him pictures from a small book of men and women. Franklin points out that was twenty-seven years ago. Chance adds that the Old Man used to visit his garden, especially after fracturing his spine thirty-five years earlier, but eventually stopped coming. Franklin says they will need proof of Chance’s residence. Chance replies, 'You have me, I am here. What more proof do you need?' Franklin and Hayes exchange uncertain looks.

Chance introduces himself as the gardener

Franklin then asked about medical records or the name of a doctor or dentist, but Chance said he had never been ill, had never left the house, and had no need for such things. He added that he had lived in the house since he was a child and had always worked in the garden. Franklin pressed him for proof of employment or residency, but Chance only repeated that he was there, that he lived there, and that he had no documents. Hayes and Franklin exchanged glances, saying nothing.

Franklin turns off the television and questions Chance's credibility

name: Chance Recalls Joe Saracini and the Old Man
description: Chance tells Franklin and Hayes about Joe Saracini, a mason who came to the house in 1952 to repair the brickwork at the rear. He remembers that Joe was fat, had short hair, and showed him pictures from a small book—images of men and women. Hayes reacts quietly. Chance also recalls the Old Man, the former homeowner, who used to visit his garden often, especially after fracturing his spine thirty-five years ago. He says the Old Man would read and rest there until he stopped coming.

name: Chance Performs His Morning Ritual
description: Chance enters the dining room, sits down at the table, turns on the television, and carefully spreads his napkin on his lap. He looks at the screen, settling into his usual routine.
related_events: Chance performs his morning dining room ritual

name: Louise Announces the Old Man's Death
description: Louise hurries down the stairs and enters the dining room, breathless and upset. She tells Chance that the Old Man has died, explaining that she found him cold and not breathing, covered him with a sheet, and called the doctor, who said he had been expecting it. Chance listens without emotion, nods, and turns back to the television. He comments on the snow falling in the garden. Louise grows angry, demanding to know if nothing he says matters, but Chance only replies that death happens to old people. She softens, apologizes for yelling, and says she doesn’t know what she expected. As she moves to prepare breakfast, she asks Chance what he will do now. He says he is going to work in the garden. She looks at him for a moment, then leaves to get him eggs. Chance changes the channel on the TV.
related_events: Louise announces the Old Man's death
Chance reacts indifferently to the news of the Old Man's death

name: Chance Comments on the Snowfall
description: Chance turns his attention back to the television, where footage shows the season's first snowfall. He remarks that it is snowing in the garden and notes that the snow is very white. Louise stands silent for a moment, then expresses frustration, demanding to know if that is all he has to say about the Old Man's death. Chance responds calmly, acknowledging that death happens to old people. After a pause, Louise softens, apologizes for yelling, and says she doesn’t know what she expected. She begins to leave, offering to make breakfast. Chance says he is very hungry. As she heads out, she asks what he plans to do now. Chance says he is going to work in the garden. Louise looks at him for a long moment, then exits. Chance nods slightly and changes the channel on the TV.
related_events: Chance comments on the snowfall in the garden

name: Louise Confronts Chance About His Indifference
description: Louise enters the dining room, breathless and upset, and tells Chance that the Old Man has died. Chance responds quietly, then turns back to the television. Louise grows agitated, saying the Old Man was cold and not breathing, and that she covered him with a sheet before calling the doctor. Chance nods and says he has seen such things before. Louise becomes angry, demanding to know if snow in the garden is all he has to say, calling his words meaningless. Chance smiles but does not reply. He acknowledges that death happens to old people. Louise sighs, sits down, and apologizes for yelling, admitting she doesn’t know what she expected. She stands and says she’ll bring him breakfast. As she heads out, she asks what he plans to do now. Chance says he will work in the garden. Louise looks at him for a moment, then leaves, saying she’ll get him some eggs. Chance nods and changes the channel on the TV.
related_events: Louise expresses anger and disappointment at Chance's reaction to the Old Man's death

name: Chance Reacts to the Old Man's Death
description: Chance sits in the dining room, watching television after spreading his napkin on his lap. Louise rushes in, breathless and upset, telling him the Old Man has died. Chance turns to her, smiles slightly, and says he has seen such things before—death happens to old people. Louise grows angry, frustrated by his lack of reaction, but then sighs and softens. She apologizes for shouting and begins to prepare breakfast. Chance mentions he is hungry. When she asks what he will do now, he says he is going to work in the garden. She looks at him for a moment, then leaves to get him eggs. Chance changes the channel on the TV.
related_events: Chance calmly accepts the Old Man's death as a natural occurrence

name: Louise Apologizes and Prepares Breakfast
description: Louise throws back the cover from a chair next to Chance and sits down, her voice quieter now. She tells Chance she doesn’t know what she expected from him and apologizes for yelling. She says it again, softer—she’s sorry. Chance doesn’t respond, his eyes still on the television. After a moment, she says she supposes she should get him some breakfast. She rises, glances toward the stairs, and mutters that at least she won’t have to stew prunes every morning anymore. At the door, she stops and asks Chance what he’s going to do now. He tells her he’s going to work in the garden. She looks at him for a long moment, then walks out, saying she’ll bring him some eggs. Chance nods and changes the channel.

name: Limo Ride to Eve's Home After Accident
description: David started the limo and pulled into traffic after the minor accident. Chance and Eve sat in the back seat, while Jeffrey took his place in the front. Eve pressed a button, closing the glass partition between the driver and the rear compartment. She then activated another mechanism, causing the limo’s bar to slide out, revealing decanters and glasses. As she poured cognac into a monogrammed crystal glass for Chance, she asked if he would like a drink, which he accepted. She introduced herself as Eve Rand, and Chance responded with his name. Eve offered to have her family doctor examine his injured leg, suggesting it would be more comfortable than going to a hospital. She instructed David to head home and asked Jeffrey to call ahead to let the household know they were coming. Jeffrey picked up the limo’s telephone and began dialing. Chance sipped the cognac, coughed slightly, and turned his attention to the television set in the limo. He reached to change the channel but paused, searching through his pockets for a remote control he did not have. Eve asked if he had lost something, and he replied that he had lost his remote. She expressed sympathy. Chance manually changed the channel and continued watching the news as David drove the limo out of Washington.

name: Chance Watches Himself on a Storefront TV
description: Chance stands in front of a store window filled with color televisions, each playing a different channel. A camera in the window broadcasts live footage of the sidewalk, and Chance notices his own image on one of the screens. He waves, lifts his arms, and moves closer and farther away, watching how his image changes. He steps back off the curb and frowns as he disappears from view. Standing between two parked cars, he takes out a remote control and points it at the TVs. Several of the sets change channels, but his image does not return to the screen.

name: Chance Pinned by Reversing Limousine
description: Chance stood between two parked cars, clicking his remote control toward the television in the store window. The limousine to his left began to back up, striking him and pinning him against the car on his right. He cried out in pain, dropping his suitcase and remote. The chauffeur, David, and the liveryman, Jeffrey, immediately jumped out of the limo and rushed to his side. David quickly moved the car forward, freeing Chance, while Jeffrey helped him onto the sidewalk. A small crowd gathered as Chance leaned against the limousine, holding his sore leg.

name: Chance Freed After Limousine Accident
description: David pulled the limousine forward, freeing Chance, who remained in pain and held his leg. Jeffrey helped him to the sidewalk as a few bystanders gathered. One of them suggested calling the police, but Chance shook his head, insisting there was no need.

name: Chance Refuses Police After Being Hit by Limo
description: A bystander suggests calling the police after Chance is pinned between two cars when a limousine backs into him. Chance, still leaning against the limo and holding his sore leg, turns toward the bystander, smiles, and says there's no need for police, explaining that it's just his leg. David, the chauffeur, offers to call an ambulance, but Chance does not respond to that suggestion. Eve Rand steps out of the limo and watches as Jeffrey helps Chance stay upright on the sidewalk.
related_events: Chance refuses police involvement despite leg injury

name: Eve Rand Steps Out and Observes the Scene

She remains silent as she watches Jeffrey attend to Chance, who leans against the car, holding his sore leg. Her presence joins the small gathering of onlookers, her gaze fixed on the man caught between the vehicles and the growing commotion around him.

name: Eve Offers Help After Chance Is Hurt
description: Jeffrey kneels to examine Chance's leg, pressing gently on a darkening bruise along his calf. Chance winces but says nothing.
